title: so we all agree that the output from all LLM are purposefully verbose to waste tokens right?
author: No_Abroad8805
selftext:
Like how many times do I have to add reminders, hooks, notes in the persistent memory... It always reverts back to firehose level of regurgitation.

Also sorry for not writing 10n paragraphs like every other post on reddit lately. I'm one of the few people that DOESN'T want to waste your time these days.

comments.author: Robonotes1760
comments.body: Try MiMo 2.6 Pro - it's very concise.

replies.author: geddy
replies.body: Is this just another model that you subscribe to, or host locally?

comments.author: Radiant_Mind33
comments.body:
That's just the nature of brute force math.

The AI isn't ever supposed to understand or remember anything. It's just supposed to keep going until it gets it right. That's why all the AI companies are subsidizing so much usage.

comments.author: SimCFB
comments.body:
It would make 0 sense for them to do it "on purpose".

Token efficiency is a major contributor to how profitable they are. That would be like McDonalds purposely pouring salt in their ice cream maker. 

In reality they do a tremendous amount of experimentation to see what gets the best results. This is what they have found works. But the problem is they do it on a large array of different problems. Your particular solution may not require so much verbosity.

comments.author: No_Abroad8805
comments.body:
I don't believe that. I believe that the market leaders (Anthropic and OpenAI) have incredibly more powerful models than what are publicly approved (still not true AI though). And let's not pretend the products we've been using haven't been lobotomised at different points in time either. 

Remember AI telling people how to make mustard gas? 

Not saying I want to make mustard gas but there's precedent for them locking knowledge and influencing the behaviour of these models.  
  
And why release the best you have when you can drip feed improvements? That's a VERY common business tactic and if AI is as great as everyone says I'm sure they are using it to inform themselves on every business practice/cash extraction method known to man.  
  
We all know a true AI would be far too dangerous in the hands of the general public so again there's precedent to believe that what we are using is actually just a carefully curated distraction machine; whose main purpose is to inflate stock prices.

comments.author: No-Market-4906
comments.body: I'm pretty sure it's because LLMs aren't good at deciding what's important so rather than trying they mostly just tell you everything they think might be relevant in the context window.
